svg.title: From source to a running stack
svg.desc: How make up turns this repository into a running stack: the build on the left, the running stack on the right, and the image's other uses below. Build, from the Dockerfile. No tests run in the image build; CI runs them. The .dockerignore allow-list lets only api/.mvn/, api/mvnw, api/pom.xml, api/src/ and web/ into the build, and they feed two stages. Stage web runs on the builder's own platform ($BUILDPLATFORM) on Node.js 24 and Alpine: npm ci with a cache at /root/.npm, then npm run build into dist/. dist/ flows into stage api, also on $BUILDPLATFORM, on the Eclipse Temurin 25 JDK and Alpine: it copies dist/ into src/main/resources/static/, runs ./mvnw -DskipTests package with a cache at /root/.m2, and extracts the jar into layers with jarmode tools. The layers flow into stage runtime, on the Eclipse Temurin 25 JRE and Alpine, which stacks four layers from least to most often changed: dependencies, spring-boot-loader, snapshot-dependencies and application. It runs as USER 10001, with TZ=UTC and a HEALTHCHECK on /readyz. The main path leads from runtime to the image branchbook:local, the highlighted node. Step 1: make up builds branchbook:local. Run, with make up: the main path continues from the image into the Docker Compose project branchbook. Service db runs PostgreSQL 17 on Alpine, with port 5432 on the compose network only, the volume db-data, and a terse error log that keeps personal data out. Step 2: db starts. A health check runs pg_isready every 2 s. Step 3: pg_isready reports db healthy. A gate, depends_on with condition service_healthy, holds service app until then. Service app runs the image branchbook:local as user 10001, with stop_grace_period 30s. Step 4: app starts; Flyway applies V1 to V7 and Hibernate validates the schema. It serves the React app at / and /assets/*, with the SPA routes forwarded to index.html; the API at /api/v1/branches, /api/v1/branches/{code}, /api/v1/branches/{code}/availability, /api/v1/appointments, /api/v1/appointments/{reference}, /api/v1/appointments/{reference}/cancel, /api/v1/messages and /api/v1/messages/{id}/retry (the simulated inbox, which compose switches on), /v3/api-docs and /swagger-ui.html; and, through Spring Boot Actuator, the probes /readyz (readiness, which includes the database) and /livez, /actuator/health, /actuator/info, and /actuator/prometheus, which serves Spring Boot's meters and the app's two, appointments_booked_total and outbox_pending. A health check, the image's HEALTHCHECK, runs wget on /readyz every 5 s after a start period of 90 s. Step 5: /readyz answers UP and the container is healthy. The main path ends at app reaching db over JDBC at db:5432; if HikariCP finds no free connection within 3 s, the API answers 503 TRY_AGAIN. A browser reaches app only through the port 127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT:-8080}. Step 6: docker compose up --wait returns and make up prints the URL. The same image elsewhere: the stack job in ci.yml builds the same image from this Dockerfile, starts it with compose up --wait, runs smoke.sh and checks the logs for credentials. A flow, cdk deploy in the ci workflow's deploy job, leads to the hosted demo's ECS Fargate task on ARM64, built by the pipeline. Developing without the image, built: make dev-api runs the API on port 8080 against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17 from Testcontainers, and make dev-web runs Vite on port 5173, proxying /api, /actuator, /readyz and /livez to port 8080. Legend: Built; Main path; Health check.
